text:
tara: rolling up polyglot-slim-v2 on staging; quick recall@10 vs maestro baseline down ~5.8% on short queries (<=6 tokens). anyone seen geometry collapse like this with newer PTQ tool?
anya: interesting. which quant profile? int5-perchannel or int6?
tara: int5-perchannel using quantize_ptq_v2 (onnx export -> per-channel scale+zero-point). int6-pc not tried yet.
mike: int5 is aggressive; could clip tail directions. try int6-pc and int8-pc for comparison.
tara: running quick eval:
```bash
python eval_embeddings.py \
  --model polyglot-slim-v2 \
  --quant int5-pc \
  --dataset short-multilang-12k \
  --metric recall@10 --batch 512
```
tara: dataset: 12,300 queries (en,fr,es,zh), median tokens 4. batching 512 to emulate prod microbatch.
jules: check tokenizer/token offsets — sometimes onnx exporter drops BOS/CLS tokens causing offsets.
kevin: also check index metric: are you using raw dot or cosine? mismatch can explain big deltas.
tara: eval harness uses cosine with pre-normalize; index built with cosine. tokenizer hashes match, but i will paste token samples.
tara: samples:
"¿Dónde está" -> [702, 13, 333]
"Where is" -> [65, 11]
ops-bot: started job embed-umap-1767781000 (staging/polyglot-slim-v2/int5) — will post when ready.
anya: please add cosine hist + l2 hist + nearest-neighbor delta stats vs maestro. a shift in mean/var is a strong clue.
ops-bot: embed-umap-1767781000 finished. summary:
- silhouette: maestro 0.51 -> polyglot-slim-v2 int5 0.34
- cosine mean (queries->gt): maestro 0.74 -> polyglot int5 0.66
- L2 norms: maestro mean 1.03,std 0.10 ; polyglot int5 mean 0.84,std 0.07 ; polyglot int8-pc mean 1.02,std 0.11
mike: that matches scale compression + variance loss. int5 quant probably collapsed smaller singular vectors.
kevin: try two quick experiments:
1) int5 + global L2 rescale (factor learned on holdout)
2) int6-pc (less aggressive) + symmetric clipping calibration
3) int5 with per-dim bias correction (post-quant)
tara: queued runs. also doing a cross-query test: build index with maestro vectors and query with polyglot-int5 to see if relative neighbors preserved.
jules: if maestro-index with polyglot-queries is still bad, geometry changed. if good, maybe index build / normalization differs.
ops-bot: quick run results (maestro-index + polyglot-int5 queries): recall@10 delta -4.9% (vs maestro->maestro baseline), so geometry shift present but slightly smaller.
anya: good sign. suggests polyglot-int5 vectors skew globally but preserve some local structure. rescale might recover most.
tara: initial rescale run recovered ~3.8% of the gap (delta now -2.0%). int6-pc run coming up.
mike: plan: short-term runtime shim that rescales embeddings for short queries and flags model for deeper quant pipeline fixes.
kevin: add an automated gate in onboarding harness: silhouette drop > 0.08 or recall@10 drop > 4% triggers manual review. Also capture l2 mean/std and cosine skew.
tara: creating ticket with scripts, plots, and ops logs. tagging @eng-platform for fallback rule: polyglot-slim-v2 should not be routed to dedicated until gate passes.
jules: tiny note: check whether we used cosine normalize in the export/serve path (some runtimes normalize on GPU float32, but quant path might skip). that causes mismatches.
tara: thanks all — will post full plots + PR for unit checks when runs complete. :heart:
